effect: A UN vote pledge no longer outlives the vote it matched. The letter says "same vote as you", but the match was tested only when accepted: the player could win a yes pledge, then vote no, and the AI stayed bound with no cost to the player. Now (1) C6B also returns the creditor, and iMQ honours a pledge unless the creditor's stored vote on that resolution differs, comparing the stored vote only (c6B), never computing it, so two countries pledged to each other cannot recurse; (2) in settlement (e6B), a pledge whose debtor voted otherwise while the creditor also left the promised vote lapses, rather than counting as broken and costing the debtor trust. A creditor who has not voted leaves the pledge binding, as today. Expected effect: only pledges whose requester changes its mind; no penalty to the AI for that. Day 0 unchanged. No new state. (Minified names in this text are those of build 26403824; the patch's find text has the current ones.)
